actionability.justification: The rule gives a concrete behavioral directive (produce exactly the requested deliverable; ask before expanding) rather than a vague aspiration, so it should visibly change what the agent does on a bounded-scope request.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: It generalizes past the two incidents to any narrow/bounded request and pairs the principle with a concrete fallback (ask before expanding) rather than stopping at a platitude like "stay in scope."

leakage.justification: No project-specific nouns (no 'cinder'/'harbor' or ticket/file identifiers) leak into the rule, though the illustrative examples ('a one-file note', 'the export only') are close paraphrases of the two source incidents rather than fully independent examples.

routing_fitness.justification: The dedup against R1-R4 is well-reasoned (verification, destructive-action, and branch-state failures are genuinely distinct from a scoping failure), and claude-md is the right cheap tier since this is a semantic judgment call not mechanically enforceable by a hook and too short to warrant a skill.

trigger_quality.justification: As a claude-md rule (not a skill) it has no formal 'Use when' trigger, and its informal condition — 'when a request names a narrow or bounded deliverable' — leaves the judgment of what counts as 'narrow' somewhat subjective.
